deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivation. It is the opening of Riemann's own published announcement (Selbstanzeige) of his 1859 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The announcement appeared in Göttinger Nachrichten 1859, No. 19, and is reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke after the memoir. The neat, regular hand suggests a fair copy made for the Werke edition, possibly not in Riemann's own hand. That would fit the editorial numeral 'IX', which replaces a struck-through earlier numeral, and the correction of 'gelehrte Anzeigen' to 'Nachrichten'.

The page makes three points:
(1) Methodological statement. The memoir is offered not as useful to experimentalists but as a contribution to the theory of nonlinear PDEs. The analogy given: the most fruitful methods for linear PDEs came from treating special physical problems with all their side conditions, not from developing the general concept. Likewise, the special problem of finite-amplitude plane air waves required new methods and viewpoints. These are, in modern terms, Riemann invariants, characteristic methods for a 2x2 hyperbolic system, and the formation of discontinuities (shocks).
(2) Historical context. The complete solution should settle the questions debated by Challis, Airy and Stokes (Phil. Mag. vols. 33-35, 1848-49), in so far as Stokes (Phil. Mag. 33, p. 349) had not already settled them. It should also settle the Vienna dispute of 1852 between Petzval, Doppler and A. von Ettingshausen (Sitzungsberichte of 15 Jan., 21 May, 1 June 1852).
(3) Physical input. The only empirical law needed beyond the general laws of motion is the adiabatic pressure-density law. In modern notation: p = phi(rho) = C*rho^k, with k = c_p/c_v (Poisson's law). Riemann says that Poisson's assumption, once poorly founded, can now be justified by Regnault's specific-heat experiments together with a principle of the mechanical theory of heat. The sentence continues on the next page.

Implicit consequence used on the following page (my addition): the sound speed is sqrt(phi'(rho)) = sqrt(k*p/rho).

results.what: Statement that the memoir is a contribution to nonlinear PDE theory, whose new methods arise from a specific physical problem
results.modern_name: Programmatic remark preceding Riemann invariants / method of characteristics / shock formation for the 1D isentropic Euler equations

results.what: Adiabatic law p proportional to rho^k with k = c_p/c_v, justified via Regnault's data and thermodynamics
results.modern_name: Poisson's adiabatic law / isentropic equation of state
results.usually_credited_to: Poisson (1823), Laplace; thermodynamic justification Clausius/Rankine c.1850

results.what: Reference to the Challis–Airy–Stokes controversy and the Petzval–Doppler–Ettingshausen dispute
results.modern_name: Historical context of the finite-amplitude sound wave debate

deep.surprise_reason: This is the published Selbstanzeige of Riemann's 1859 shock-wave paper, printed in Göttinger Nachrichten and in his Werke; the page appears to be a fair copy of it. It contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: For p = C*rho^k, dp/drho = k*p/rho, so the sound speed is sqrt(k*p/rho).

The velocity function from the next page, ∫ sqrt(phi'(rho)) dlog(rho), equals 2*c/(k-1) for the Poisson law (Riemann invariant). The expression should simplify to 0; this needs k > 1 (k != 1) to hold.
Using c = 332.37 m/s at 0 °C gives k ≈ 1.41 (cf. the 1.4095 on the next page). Exact agreement depends on the density and pressure values used.

transcription_corrections: The struck-through numeral above 'IX' is uncertain (reads 'XVI' or 'XII').
'(Göttinger ~~gelehrte Anzeigen~~ Nachrichten, 1859, ~~...~~. No 19)': 'Nachrichten' is inserted above the struck words; the struck item after 1859 is illegible.
'lebhaft verhandelten Fragen 1)' carries a superscript footnote marker 1) (written like '#' / '1)' after 'Stokes'); the transcription is otherwise accurate.
The page appears to be a fair copy in a hand other than Riemann's, consistent with editorial preparation of the Werke.
